title: ARIA AP receiver identity response, statement type aria-ap-identity/1 (provisional: pending decision D3)
description: A receiver's answer to GET /.well-known/aria/identity?nonce&audience: its AID 1.0 document and a statement bound to the client's nonce, carrying a single-use challenge for the client's next request. Provisional: the transport is not decided, and this schema changes with it. Conforming to it does not authenticate the receiver: a client also verifies the document under its trusted issuers, checks it is the credential the statement names, pins the receiver's DID and origin, matches its own audience and nonce, checks freshness, verifies the Ed25519 signature by that credential's holder key over the canonical JSON of the statement without proof.value, and requires the credential's status to be good now.

credential.description: The exact credential instance whose holder key signs.

origin.description: The origin the receiver is reached at, in canonical form: https://host[:port], or http:// on a loopback host for local use; a lower-case DNS name whose last label starts with a letter, or a dotted-quad IPv4 address; no default port, path, query, fragment or user information. The pattern is syntax only: the value must also parse as a URL whose serialization is the value itself, valid IDNA included (https://xn--a.example matches the pattern and is not an origin); the ARIA AP SDK checks this.

audience.description: The client the statement is for.

nonce.description: The client's nonce, as sent: base64url.

challenge.description: Single use, short lived: the nonce of the client's next signed request.

created.description: RFC 3339 in UTC to the second, a date that exists; the client accepts it for 60 seconds. The format must be asserted (for example Ajv with ajv-formats).
